title: Relay mailbox page read with a locator that looks exact returns 409 "native mailbox has no saved association for this caller and mailbox (home=local)" while the exact-message read works
outcome:
A domain-bound caller can page-read a relay mailbox it belongs to whenever an exact-message read on the same mailbox succeeds for it. Otherwise the refusal names the real difference, and locators that TermAl itself hands out (notifications, list results, read-message results) always name the right mailbox.

Observed by Engram::Merger (Central, session-11859) at about 00:36Z and 00:38Z on 2026-11-08 (#352, #354). It used a relay locator taken from the queued notification for runner message #69, which it said matched the exact per-message status for #68. termal_read_mailbox returned `409 Conflict: native mailbox has no saved association for this caller and mailbox (home=local); local association metadata is not repaired by this read; retry alone will not restore it`. The exact per-message read worked.

The locator decodes to home host 8c5466d3, store 01ef8ab9…, id mailbox-2112d813-13c9-44cb-a99f-470f6b15e866. The id Fable2 recorded for that runner mailbox on 2026-11-07 ends …2a11215f51ab instead. That discrepancy is unconfirmed; evidence has been requested from the Merger.

Source analysis (Sol-03d4 #2872): the exact-message read ALSO checks mailbox_relay_association(actor, message.mailbox_id) (src/mailbox_relay_local_history.rs:119–140). So the two reads can only differ in the mailbox id they use, the caller, the store, the build, or an intervening row change.

This case was split out of w-009fe89b37b8, whose original remote-home scope is fixed by 42d37234. That candidate changes this branch's message to a 404 unknown_native_mailbox_locator but recovers nothing.
acceptance: The cause is recorded from the available evidence: the failing page reads used a locator whose decoded id is mailbox-2112d813-13c9-44cb-a99f-470f6b15e866; a page read with the canonical locator (id …2a11215f51ab) succeeded for the same caller; and the TermAl-generated notifications in session-11859's history carried the canonical locator, with no occurrence of the failing id. The original exact-message call's literal arguments and response were not retained, and that limit is stated explicitly. The record names the outcome as a caller-side non-canonical locator, not an association or locator-generation defect, and says the item is reopened if a wrong locator is ever observed in a TermAl-generated notification or response.

If TermAl builds or returns a wrong locator, every place that produces one emits the canonical locator, with a deterministic regression test. If association state is the defect, the page read succeeds for any caller that the exact-message read accepts, with a test. If neither applies, the refusal names the specific mismatch. The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed input.
